scientific_bottom_line.behavioral_process: Recent-rain contrasts are associated with activation of previously silent species x stop cells, including direct transitions to overlapping/full chorus states.
scientific_bottom_line.ecological_memory: Most rainfall-associated route-new incidence and strong/full-chorus activation is recurrent in the historical acoustic record, especially at the same physical SiteID.
scientific_bottom_line.spatial_template: Within focal pair x species, historically strong SiteIDs are much more likely to host later wet-survey strong/full chorus, identifying a stable local spatial template of acoustic activity.
scientific_bottom_line.unresolved_generator: Strictly-prior local-memory probabilities, route-cross-fit species rainfall sensitivity, dry-state persistence, and one cross-fit rain x local-memory gate still fail to reproduce the observed four-component matrix allocation.
scientific_bottom_line.interpretation: The data identify structured state-dependent reactivation of a latent acoustic network, but do not identify a sufficient unique lower-level biological generator.
scientific_bottom_line.universality: Strong within-NAAMP geographic robustness is supported, but state effects are heterogeneous and direct cross-continental matrix replication is unavailable; universality is not established.

geographic_generality.interpretation: Robust at programme scale but strongly heterogeneous among states.

spatial_depth.interpretation: Once recruited, route-new taxa deepen spatial participation more than expected; occupied-stop placement metrics do not justify a simple geographic-hotspot mechanism.

opportunity_normalized_rain_memory.interpretation: Rain contrast selectively favors historically recurrent full-chorus opportunities even when recurrent and nonrecurrent candidate-cell counts are normalized.

memory_age.formal_gate_reason: 433 informative pair-species groups but only 136 routes; prefixed requirement was >=200 routes.
memory_age.interpretation: Durable-memory formal classification withheld; diagnostic evidence suggests multi-year persistence with decay.

stopping_rule.decision: STOP lower-level mechanism escalation after final held-out rain-by-memory gating null rejection.
prohibited: No arbitrary site-specific rainfall coefficients learned and tested on the same routes.
No RC11 submission modification from these exploratory analyses.

final_ecological_statement: Rainfall-associated acoustic expansion primarily reactivates a historically recurrent, site-structured chorus network: previously silent species x site cells often return at overlapping or full-chorus intensity, and historically strong SiteIDs predict where reactivation occurs. Yet the full taxonomic-versus-spatial allocation remains more structured than species sensitivity, prior local memory, dry persistence, and one held-out rain-by-memory gate can generate. The public observational data therefore support structured latent-network reactivation but do not identify a sufficient unique lower-level mechanism.
final_generality_statement: Within NAAMP the process is taxonomically diffuse, insensitive to single-state omission, observer turnover, stop relocation and measured acoustic conditions, but state-specific effects are heterogeneous. Direct cross-continental replication of the full species x site matrix geometry remains unavailable, so universality is not established.
